findings.title: Plain Error thrown instead of TRPCError
findings.body: When the credential is not found or belongs to another user, the handler throws a plain Error. tRPC turns this into a 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR instead of a NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN response, so an ordinary access-denied case is reported as a server failure. Throw a TRPCError with an appropriate code instead.

findings.title: updateMany with empty data likely does not bump updatedAt
findings.body: `updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` sends empty update data. Prisma may skip the query or never set `@updatedAt`, so SelectedCalendar.updatedAt is not reliably refreshed. This adds a write on every cache refresh while the UI never reads that field. Either drop the call or set `updatedAt: new Date()` explicitly.

findings.title: connectedCalendars not invalidated after cache deletion
findings.body: The delete-cache mutation does not invalidate `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`, and the query uses `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`. After a successful delete, the dropdown keeps showing the stale 'Last updated' timestamp and the delete action until the page is reloaded.

findings.title: Hardcoded en-US date formatting
findings.body: The cache timestamp is formatted with `Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US")` even though the surrounding string is localized. Non-English users therefore see US-style dates. Use the user's locale from `useLocale`.

findings.title: BSD-only sed -i syntax
findings.body: `sed -i ''` is macOS/BSD syntax. On GNU/Linux sed the empty string is read as a script or file argument and the command fails, so the env file is never updated.

findings.title: Error alert now hides remove action when connection modification is disabled
findings.body: Previously the error Alert showed the disconnect button whenever the credential was not delegated, regardless of `disableConnectionModification`. It now passes `disableConnectionModification`, so in that mode users with a broken calendar can no longer remove it. This is a behavior change the PR does not mention.
